name: Shadow-maw
reason: The source's awkward machine-translated creature name 'Tuna Bird' was renamed 'Shadow-maw' to give the cave predators a menacing Western fantasy register.
description: Winged predatory beasts that infest the Dark Nether Cave (Eps 637-678). They attack in agile swarms of ten or more, far faster in the air than human warriors, and use eerie calls to summon reinforcements; despite their menace they sit near the bottom of the cave's food chain, and a far larger tongue-lashing monster sweeps them up like flies. Corresponds to the source's 'Tuna Birds' in the Mysterious/Profound Nether Cave, including the giant toad's tongue scene (chs ~620-625).

name: Evil Dragon
reason: The source's English term 'Evil Dragon' was carried over unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: The antithesis of the Ancestral Dragon: a manifestation of the darkness within the dragon race, described as a kind of living Hell (Eps 912-954). A young Evil Dragon erupts during the Wade/Resetter incident, shattering restraints and rampaging while Max and four others struggle to contain it. Matches the source's Evil Dragon that appears opposite the Ancestral Dragon in the Heavenly Stellar Holy Land arc and is hunted by the Demi-Immortal Clan (chs ~895-905).

name: Connor
issues: MERGED NAME: 'Connor' names two different characters. Eps 347-349: the Seventh Prince (source Su Xing), harp-playing rival of Ray for the throne. Eps 44-126: a different Connor, youngest son of House Sterling and Felix's brother (source counterpart Zhuge Hong, the Gauntlet roadblock ringleader Zane grabs by the throat). These should be tracked as separate entities.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Connor' was chosen as a polished, aristocratic-sounding name befitting the scheming Seventh Prince.
description: The Seventh Prince, chief rival of Ray (the Third Prince, source Su Rui) in the struggle for the throne (Eps 347-349). A cold political schemer who plays the harp, wears a purple hat, and is flanked by extremely fast guards; like Ray, he dares not strike the Crown Prince first for fear of being branded a traitor. Matches the source's Seventh Prince Su Xing, who is backed by a group of old eunuchs (chs ~330-336). Note: the name 'Connor' was also used earlier (Eps 44-126) for an unrelated House Sterling youth.

name: House
reason: Generic capitalized common noun referring to the Legacy Houses (House Lowell, House Warrick, etc.), which are tracked as their own entities; not a distinct entity itself.

name: Seven-Star Platform
reason: The source's clunky translated term 'Seven Stars Spectroscopic Platform' (also rendered 'Seven Stars Sword Radiance Platform') was streamlined to 'Seven-Star Platform' for readability.
description: A wave-based combat training arena within the Skyreach Sect, with multiple entrances, difficulty levels, and magic arrays (Eps 222-226; Finn later trains there in Ep 350). Disciples test themselves against escalating waves; Zane comprehends sword intent there, and clearing higher waves marks elite talent. Corresponds to the source's Seven Stars Spectroscopic Platform where Luo Zheng passes the eighth level and gains Sword Intent (chs ~213-271).

name: Darcy
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Darcy' evokes a haughty young aristocrat; the surname 'Hawthorne' was assigned to his newly risen house (source Huang Family) to keep the family unit consistent.
description: Young master of House Hawthorne, a newly powerful house in Castermere County, and a fifth grade Adept (Eps 326-336). Miles Lowell fawns over him and beats Melvin on his behalf, provoking the confrontation in which Zane kills Darcy at Lowell Manor; his father Chuck is later maimed and forced to compensate House Lowell. Matches the source's Huang Xing of the Huang Family in Chongyang County, whom Luo Peihao (Miles) flatters while Luo Dalong (Melvin) insults the upstart family (chs ~317-318).

name: Celestial Tomb of Vesper
reason: The source term 'Heavenly Mist Immortal Tomb' (variously rendered 'Sky Mist' / 'Heaven Mist Immortal Tomb') was renamed 'Celestial Tomb of Vesper' to give the immortal's resting place a more evocative Western fantasy name.
description: The sealed resting place of a fallen immortal, named to preserve his legacy after his consciousness scattered to the void (Eps 400-799). Opening it requires nine Enchanted Lamps, and nine major powers - including the Cloud Hall, the World Merchants' Guild, Bloodwood Cliff, the Mysterious Luna Hall, and the Black Mountain Order - descend upon it, suppressed to a fraction of their cultivation inside. Corresponds to the source's Heavenly Mist Immortal Tomb in the Central Domain, a cursed, barrier-protected tomb and a great opportunity for warriors (chs ~388-931).

name: Message Rune
reason: The source term 'Sound Transmitting Talisman' was renamed 'Message Rune' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: A consumable magical item used to send short voice messages across distances; it whispers its message into the recipient's ear and burns to ash once delivered (Eps 406-1117). Tia uses them for covert coordination, and in the Lower World even the most powerful Message Rune only carries about thirty thousand miles. Corresponds to the source's Sound Transmitting Talisman (chs ~408-1110).

name: Fighting Soul
reason: The source term 'Combat Soul' (a soul-cultivation realm) was localized as 'Fighting Soul' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A high soul-cultivation level that no one in the Eastern Territories had ever awakened before Zane (Eps 441-900). Zane attains it while still only in the Adept Realm - a shocking mismatch between body and soul cultivation - and it renders him immune to soul attacks such as the Skull Ghost Hand. Corresponds to the source's Combat Soul realm, which Luo Zheng breaks through to at Dragonfall Palace to Palace Lord Long Yuan's astonishment (chs ~429-877).

name: Greater Lotus Flower
reason: The source's Buddhist term 'Mahayana Lotus Flower' was renamed 'Greater Lotus Flower' (with 'Hinayana' becoming 'Lesser Lotus Flower') to strip the real-world religious vocabulary while keeping the greater/lesser pairing.
description: The rarer, superior form of the soul lotus opened upon entering the Life-and-Death Realm: where the Lesser Lotus Flower has nine petals, the Greater Lotus Flower has far more - 29 in the source (Eps 884-1300). Zane activates one at only the fifth level of the Life-and-Death Realm, stunning observers; a palace lord's own Greater Lotus bloomed just five petals on her tenth tribulation. Corresponds to the source's Mahayana Lotus Flower (chs ~861-1305).

name: Auspice City
reason: The source's transliterated place name 'Zeji City' was localized as 'Auspice City' to replace the pinyin with a meaningful Western-style city name.
description: A major city where several secret human sects, including the Radiant Light Sect, gather believers and accumulate Faith Energy (Eps 1123-1166). Zane's group regroups there at Lincoln's designated spot and gears up to face whatever waits in the dark beneath the city. Aligns with the source's Zeji City, where the Purple Bamboo Sacred Land maintains its Ginkgo Pavilion front (chs ~1103-1146).

name: Ryder
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Ryder' was chosen as a brash, competitive-sounding name for the rival weapon-seeker.
description: A proud cultivator competing in the Divine Weapon Hall's sword-selection trial overseen by the white-eyebrowed elder (Eps 1045-1052). Ruthlessly ambitious, he eyes four of the swords at once, gambles 'all or nothing' on the ascent, and relies on raw willpower when the mounting gravity nears his limit. Matches the source's Xie Mang of Misty Cloud Palace, elder brother of Xie Jun, in the divine artifact selection (chs ~1022-1029).

name: Alex Gresham
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Alex Gresham' gives the arrogant young noble a crisp, patrician-sounding full name; his Gongsun family became a Third-Grade House.
description: Eldest son of a Third-Grade House in Oracle City, a Heaven-level talent at the Inner-Core Realm and a minor celebrity of the tournament pre-qualifiers (Eps 484-486). A practitioner of the Twin-Sword School who flourishes paired blades in flashes of golden radiance, he is condescending toward Zane but is defeated by him in a single strike. Matches the source's Gongsun Zhen, the Dual Sword Style fighter from a third-rank family with Heaven Grade talent whom Luo Zheng beats in the Martial Arts Conference (chs ~473-477).

name: Benson
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Benson' was chosen as a solid, confident name for the Cloud Hall's champion disciple.
description: The Cloud Hall's strongest Inner-Core Realm disciple, a Celestial-level talent who fights with water techniques such as the Water Tornado and a Sea God invocation (Eps 491-496). Eager to knock the independent fighter Eden Caldwell down a peg, he challenges him in the tournament arena but is ultimately forced to surrender. Matches the source's Xuanyuan Xiao of the Cloud Hall, matched against 'independent cultivator Cui Yun' (Luo Zheng's alias) in the 33rd match (chs ~472-483).

name: Scott
reason: The character's translated royal title 'Sky Fortune King' was replaced by the personal US-origin name 'Scott' to simplify the source's title-heavy naming for the audio format.
description: A king-level ruler from the Star Field Divine Kingdom who attends the great gathering of Divine Kingdom sovereigns alongside figures like War Emperor York and War King Wind (Eps 799-912). Boisterous and outwardly kindly where York is grimly silent, he smiles even at a kneeling subordinate's failure, but argues forcefully in the later deliberations over Zane's fate. Matches the source's Sky Fortune King of the Star Field Divine Kingdom, who champions his kingdom's disciples in the inter-kingdom contests (chs ~776-874).

name: Dalton
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Dalton' was chosen as a sturdy, dependable name for the veteran swordsman ally.
description: A Varsity-rank swordsman wielding Twin Blades who fights in the demon war at Zane's side, where Zane's feats renew his fighting spirit mid-battle against a demon general (Eps 116-128, with later appearances to Ep 485). He leads a group of allied disciples, holding back the Stormcrown disciples and preferring to unsettle opponents like Josef with words before blades. Tentatively corresponds to the source's Lin Geng, the strong senior sword disciple who leads Xiao Yufeng's team through the demon-infested arc (chs ~97-220); the match is plausible but unconfirmed.

name: Sterling
reason: The source's aristocratic 'Family Zhuge' was localized as 'House Sterling', a cold, moneyed-sounding Western surname, in line with the show's 'Legacy House' naming convention.
description: A powerful Legacy House and running early antagonist faction to Zane (Eps 44-941). Its members include Connor (the Gauntlet ringleader), family leader Felix, Preston, and the Imperial Army counselor Josef, whose Sterling backing makes him nearly untouchable; a Sterling family heirloom serves as a last-resort life-saving treasure. Corresponds to the source's Family Zhuge, one of the great noble clans - Zhuge Hong, Third Young Master Zhuge Feng, and their Imperial Army connections (chs ~28-238).

name: Crystal Butterfly
issues: Ep 1135's 'Ice Crystal Butterfly' (a ranked venomous beast whose freezing poison traps souls in ice) is a different entity accidentally folded into this item's mentions by substring match.
reason: The source term 'Jade Butterfly' was renamed 'Crystal Butterfly' to match the adaptation's crystal-themed item vocabulary.
description: A butterfly-shaped treasure blade of Zane's, powered in the source by a Soaring Phoenix Crystal (Eps 142-672). Beyond serving as a weapon, it acts as a guide: in the Dark Nether Cave arc Zane follows the Crystal Butterfly, which lights up as he nears his objective, and others recognize it as a significant treasure. Corresponds to the source's Jade Butterfly blade carried by Luo Zheng (chs ~128-646).

name: Murry Cook
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Murry Cook' was chosen as an unassuming bureaucratic name for the corrupt sect judge.
description: The presiding judge of the Skyreach Sect's Hall of Judgment, who schemes to have Zane beaten to death under cover of sect law rather than kill him outright (Eps 168-176). When Zane mocks the Hall of Judgment, Murry seizes the excuse to act, ultimately tracing a deadly 'Kill' sigil in the air with his brush pen. Matches the source's Qin Mu, judge of the Hall of Precepts, who writes a giant 'Kill' character with his Magistrate Pen and attacks Luo Zheng (chs ~154-162).

name: Jill
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Jill' was chosen as a light, deceptively sweet name for the slight but lethal swordswoman.
description: A slight but deceptively quick swordswoman wielding an Emerald Sword in the sect tournament (Eps 235-236, discussed through Ep 342). Smiling almost angelically throughout her bouts, she upsets expectations by defeating the big poison-specialist Benjamin and builds a winning streak that others vow to end. Matches the source's Quan Xiaoyan of Jade Maiden Peak, the cute, smiling eighteen-year-old prodigy who darts through Long Bin's energy rings to beat him in the Peak Competition (chs ~222-329).

name: Guardian
issues: The surface 'Guardian' also appears inside distinct entities (the 'Immovable Guardian' of Patrick's palm technique, source Acalanatha; the 'Seal of the Guardian'; the 'Guardian Locket' item), which should not be conflated with the sect rank.
reason: 'Guardian' is the adaptation's term for a senior protector rank in the Skyreach Sect hierarchy; no specific source-novel term for this rank was identified in the evidence.
description: A senior rank of protector within the Skyreach Sect, standing above ordinary disciples and just below the elders (Eps 260-971). Guardians are powerful enough that a rising genius closing on their level is remarkable, and even they and the elders compete desperately for the sect's few yearly draughts; one Guardian brings his palm down on Lily like a hammer in Ep 314.

name: Stanley
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Stanley' was chosen as a cool, calculating-sounding name for the fan-wielding inner disciple.
description: An inner disciple who fights with the Gold Flower Fan, a Spirit Weapon whose unfolded edges cut sharper than blades, and the Golden Razornet technique that weaves golden threads into an entangling net (Eps 261-263). Cold and calculating, he baits his opponent like a fish on a hook, but Jacob outclasses him in every way and steamrolls him from the start. Matches the source's Pu Xingyu, who wields a golden fan and a golden-thread net against Wang Yun in the Peak Competition (chs ~249-253).

name: Ken Lowell
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Ken' was chosen as a plain family-elder name, with the surname 'Lowell' keeping him inside Zane's family unit.
description: A senior member of House Lowell and father of Andrew, the son who once tried to kill Zane with the copied Stormbreaker Halberd (Eps 326-335). Brother to Bryson, whose secret pact with the imprisoned Blood Prisoner horrifies him, Ken grows desperate enough during the family conflict to unleash the Stormkill Halberd - a three-charge mechanical heirloom no Lowell had dared use for decades. Matches the source's Luo Junyi, whose eldest son Luo Chengyun fought Luo Zheng to the death with the halberd's replica, and who then wields the true Thousand Forms Tribulation Thunder Halberd himself (chs ~317-325).

name: Duskfall Sect
reason: The source's 'Misty Cloud Sect' - one of several similarly named cloud sects - was renamed 'Duskfall Sect' to keep the competing sects audibly distinct in the audio adaptation.
description: A sect competing in the Cloud Road Trial, counting Adler and Randy among its members; Adler, one of its top disciples, placed third in The Crimson Crucible (Eps 361-404). Its disciples fare poorly in the fiery trial - one missteps and plunges a foot into the lava - and its sect head looks grim while others celebrate the trial's outcome. Matches the source's Misty Cloud Sect, whose top disciple (surnamed Pang) entered the smelting trial as a third-place finisher and whose junior brother was burned in the lava sea (chs ~350-355).

name: Lennon
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name. 'Lennon Anderson' was chosen as a sharp, modern-sounding full name for the elite squad leader.
description: The strongest of the Cloud Hall's new disciples, leading a squad of twelve elite cultivators through the Cloud Road Trial (Eps 367-407). He commands the Formation of the Twelve Signs powering the Scythe of the River-Winds - a technique requiring all thirteen members including himself - fights with a Green Caltrop Pike, and pushes through severe burns in pursuit of the blue treasure box and its Lifeblood. Matches the source's Zhao Xiaohua, one of the Cloud Hall's top two disciples (with Zhuo Bufan) and the one who presided over the Cloud Hall's large array in the hidden trial (chs ~354-394).

name: Sky-Reaver
reason: The source's Buddhist-mythology creature 'Flying Yaksha' was renamed 'Sky-Reaver' to remove the real-world religious reference while keeping the airborne-menace flavor.
description: Powerful golden-bodied aerial creatures guarding the Path of Death trial; a direct fight with one risks drawing other dangerous creatures (Eps 383-412). One finishes Patrick off with three brutal blows after a long struggle, and Zane later judges its golden form a step above even his Spirit Weapon-grade body. Matches the source's Flying Yakshas, one of which Pei Tianyao slays alone before being defeated by the others (chs ~374-376).

name: Cosmic Spirit Index
reason: The source term 'Universal Myriad Spirit Stele' was renamed 'Cosmic Spirit Index' to turn the unwieldy stele name into a clean ranking-list concept for Western listeners.
description: The most famous ranking of magical weapons across the universes; when a Sovereign-grade Divine Weapon appears, it is sensed and its name enters the list (Eps 978-1311). Top-tier weaponsmith clans are measured by whether their creations can shift its rankings, and entries range from reality-bending Divine Weapons to the purely destructive Saint-Killing Spear; one sword Zane encounters ranks second. Corresponds to the source's Universal Myriad Spirit Stele (chs ~955-1291).
